LP011: `d=(-2,1,0)` and `q=(1,4,3)` both map to the same min-zero tuple `(0,3,2)`, but their native signed absolute-dominant axes are respectively `(axis 0, negative)` and `(axis 1, positive)`. Thus a historical min-zero inverse `M=max(A,B,C)` cannot itself serve as an all-signed native dominance caller. This is a small reproducible witness and consumes the previously established signed chamber theorem.

LP019: on a `1×1` positive two-generator grid the paths `HV` and `VH` have one terminal but are **two** Path-formal witnesses. Their incidence-chain difference is a signed square circuit with coefficients `(+1,+1,-1,-1)` and zero boundary. The signs refer to the **difference of graph chains**; the positive endpoint N-BRC is `2`, Boolean support is `1`, not an algebraically cancelled zero. In the full signed six-axis step alphabet, precisely **12** ordered length-two native words `(+e_i,-e_i)` / `(-e_i,+e_i)` return to the starting Cell; the positive monotone 1×1 graph admits no such length-two return. This tests the scope of the graph consumer, without asserting that native zero has shortest-path count 12 (its shortest path is the empty word).
